thesis: Deterra Royalties is an ASX-listed passive royalty company that receives cash from mining operators without operating mines or bearing production capital spending. **[Fact]** The cornerstone asset is a **1.232%** gross revenue royalty over BHP's Mining Area C (MAC) iron ore hub in Western Australia, plus **A$1 million** capacity payments per million dry metric tonnes of annual production increase (`DRR.AX/investor-documents/official-reports/250325-1HY25-Deterra-Royalties-Financial-Results-Declaration.pdf`). **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **A$263.4 million** (+10%); underlying EBITDA **A$250 million** (+10%); net profit after tax **A$155.7 million**; total dividends **22 cents** per share fully franked (`DRR.AX/investor-documents/asx-announcements/2931000.pdf`). **[Fact]** At 31 December 2024, net assets were **19.1 cents** per share while net tangible assets were **(42.1) cents** per share because royalty intangibles are excluded from NTA (same half-year report). **[Fact]** Net debt at 30 June 2025 was **A$271 million** with **A$205 million** undrawn on **A$500 million** credit facilities (FY25 results presentation).
why_market_wrong: The market may treat Deterra as a single-commodity iron ore yield stock and miss the option stack in Thacker Pass lithium (first production late 2027) and the gold offtake book acquired via Trident. **[Inference]** FY2025 gold offtake net revenue margin was **A$21.5 million** on record gold prices, diversifying cash away from MAC iron ore alone. **[Inference]** The 1H25 interim dividend cut to **9 cents** (from **14.89 cents** in 1H24) may anchor yield screens on a trough payout rather than the **75% of NPAT** policy confirmed at FY25. Index and domestic yield buyers may underweight ASX royalty structures relative to US trust equivalents (MSB, SJT).
